sentences.en: That is the talking stage, that kind of murky, unlabeled limbo where you're messaging someone like every single day, you're flirting, you're sharing things, but you're not dating.
sentences.zh: 那就是“暧昧期”，那种模糊不清、没有标签的边缘地带，你每天都在和某人发消息，调情，分享生活，但你们并没有在约会。

sentences.en: Maybe you haven't even met in person yet.
sentences.zh: 也许你们甚至还没见过面。

sentences.en: You're not really sure where things are going or if they're going anywhere at all.
sentences.zh: 你并不确定事情会走向何方，或者是否会有任何进展。

sentences.en: Yet, it's this strange thing where this person has become part of your daily life.
sentences.zh: 然而，这是一种奇怪的状态，这个人已经成为了你日常生活的一部分。

sentences.en: You're kind of expecting things from them.
sentences.zh: 你甚至会对他们产生某种期待。

sentences.en: So why do we even have a talking stage?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们为什么会有暧昧期呢？

sentences.en: And why has it become so psychologically intense as of recent?
sentences.zh: 为什么它最近在心理上变得如此强烈？

sentences.en: We're going to break down the psychology behind this today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们将剖析这背后的心理学。

sentences.en: Specifically, what makes a talking stage so compelling?
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是什么让暧昧期如此令人着迷？

sentences.en: Why do we get attached without even knowing someone?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们在还没了解对方的情况下就会产生依恋？

sentences.en: How do we protect ourselves from emotionally investing in people that we are interested in while still being open to communicating?
sentences.zh: 我们如何在保持沟通开放的同时，保护自己不向感兴趣的人投入过多的情感？

sentences.en: Lots of big questions there.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多大问题。

sentences.en: We're also going to look at the personality traits of people who extend and love a prolonged talking stage.
sentences.zh: 我们还将看看那些延长并享受长期暧昧期的人的性格特征。

sentences.en: Perhaps the people you should be avoiding and the role of certain traits like commitment readiness,
sentences.zh: 也许是那些你应该避开的人，以及某些特质的作用，比如承诺准备度、

sentences.en: intermittent reinforcement.
sentences.zh: 间歇性强化。

sentences.en: And also, this is a big message for this episode, why playing games, game playing in the talking stage is basically going to instantaneously mean
sentences.zh: 而且，这也是本期节目的一个重要信息，为什么在暧昧期玩心理游戏基本上意味着

sentences.en: that you are not going to be in a relationship with that person.
sentences.zh: 你将无法与那个人建立真正的关系。

sentences.en: We need to be pursuing authenticity, especially in this current dating environment where, you know, dating apps give us the illusion of endless choices and endless possibilities
sentences.zh: 我们需要追求真实，特别是在当前这种约会环境下，你知道，约会软件给了我们一种拥有无限选择和无限可能的错觉，

sentences.en: and no one wants to commit, no one wants to go on dates.
sentences.zh: 而没有人愿意承诺，没有人愿意去约会。

sentences.en: Being authentic and direct about what you want is the only way.
sentences.zh: 真诚并直接地表达你的需求是唯一的出路。

sentences.en: So, if you have ever felt stuck in a never-ending talking stage, you are not alone.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你曾经感到困在没完没了的暧昧期中，你并不孤单。

sentences.en: I have been there, done that, got the t-shirt as have many other people in their 20s, but we're going to unpack it today.
sentences.zh: 我经历过，做过，也像许多其他20多岁的人一样深陷其中，但今天我们要把它拆解开来。

sentences.en: All of the psychology as well as a little bit of a guide to getting through the talking stage, how to find closure when the talking stage perhaps ends and my hard and fast rules
sentences.zh: 所有的心理学知识，以及一点点度过暧昧期的指南，当暧昧期结束时如何寻找终结感，以及我的硬性规定，

sentences.en: for exactly how long you should be chatting with someone before you go on a date.
sentences.zh: 关于在去约会之前你应该和某人聊多久。

sentences.en: So, with all of that in mind, stay with us.
sentences.zh: 所以，带着这些想法，请继续收听。

sentences.en: So, I want to begin by kind of defining some parameters here.
sentences.zh: 那么，我想先定义一些参数。

sentences.en: The talking stage for me, I know it has a few different ways of being thought about, but for me, it is the stage before you officially go on a date.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，暧昧期，我知道人们有几种不同的看法，但对我而言，它是你正式去约会之前的阶段。

sentences.en: It's the lead-up, it's the preamble, it may also sometimes last past the first, I would say, two dates if there is long gaps between when you are going on dates
sentences.zh: 这是前奏，是铺垫，有时它甚至可能持续到第一次约会之后，如果你们约会之间有很长的间隔，

sentences.en: in which you are talking.
sentences.zh: 而你们在这期间一直保持着联系。

sentences.en: But it's really that period where you're on each other's radar, but you're not consistently dating.
sentences.zh: 但它确实是你们互相关注，但并没有持续约会的那段时期。

sentences.en: You're not planning for dates, date one or date two or date three.
sentences.zh: 你们没有在计划约会，无论是第一次、第二次还是第三次。

sentences.en: So, essentially, the defining feature of a talking stage is you are spending the majority of your time communicating with them over messenger, over text, online, and not much time
sentences.zh: 所以，本质上，暧昧期的定义特征是你大部分时间都在通过通讯软件、短信、在线与他们交流，而没有花太多时间

sentences.en: making concrete plans or seeing each other in real life, which I think we can all agree is really preferable.
sentences.zh: 制定具体的计划或在现实生活中见面，我想我们都会同意，现实见面才是真正可取的。

sentences.en: Let's talk about this.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈这个。

sentences.en: Why do we even have a talking stage to begin with if most people's experience of it is awful and less than pleasant?
sentences.zh: 如果大多数人的体验都很糟糕且不愉快，我们为什么还要有暧昧期呢？

sentences.en: Well, essentially, the talking stage is part of what we call our modern dating script.
sentences.zh: 嗯，本质上，暧昧期是我们所谓的“现代约会剧本”的一部分。

sentences.en: So, the modern dating script is basically the storyline we all expect a romance to follow.
sentences.zh: 所以，现代约会剧本基本上是我们所有人都期望浪漫关系遵循的故事线。

sentences.en: It's the script that influences how you believe you should interact at certain times, what your timeline should be, and it kind of goes like this.
sentences.zh: 它是影响你认为在特定时间应该如何互动、你的时间表应该是什么样的剧本，它大致是这样的：

sentences.en: You cross paths, you spend some time talking to figure each other out, then you go on a date, go on a few more dates, wait a few months, make sure they're not seeing other people,
sentences.zh: 你们相遇，花时间聊天来了解对方，然后去约会，再多约会几次，等上几个月，确保他们没有和其他人见面，

sentences.en: make sure you're not seeing other people, and hopefully you end up in a relationship.
sentences.zh: 确保你没有和其他人见面，希望最终你们能建立起一段关系。

sentences.en: During each stage or chapter of that, there are different ways of communicating and interacting with each other that we kind of pick up from media, culture, society at large.
sentences.zh: 在这一过程的每个阶段或章节中，都有不同的沟通和互动方式，我们从媒体、文化、整个社会中习得这些方式。

sentences.en: Of course, ending up in a relationship, most of us would be able to tell this is not always the case.
sentences.zh: 当然，最终建立关系，我们大多数人都能看出这并不总是事实。

sentences.en: At every stage of this script or this narrative, there is a way for things to get complicated.
sentences.zh: 在这个剧本或叙事的每个阶段，事情都有可能变得复杂。

sentences.en: The talking stage is no different.
sentences.zh: 暧昧期也不例外。

sentences.en: In some cultures and countries, like, there is no talking stage.
sentences.zh: 在某些文化和国家，比如，根本没有暧昧期。

sentences.en: That's just not part of their dating script.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是他们约会剧本的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, the only talking that gets done is asking someone to go out immediately.
sentences.zh: 你知道，唯一的交流就是直接邀请某人出去。

sentences.en: But it's definitely becoming a more prominent part of how we view dating.
sentences.zh: 但它确实正在成为我们看待约会方式中更突出的部分。

sentences.en: And actually, this generation, more than any other, take longer to decide if they want to date someone.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这一代人比以往任何一代人都要花更长的时间来决定他们是否想和某人约会。

sentences.en: A 2024 study, it was one of the first to really investigate the talking stage.
sentences.zh: 2024年的一项研究，是首批真正调查暧昧期的研究之一。

sentences.en: It found that the talking stage is what they would call a new relationship construct.
sentences.zh: 它发现暧昧期是他们所称的一种“新的关系结构”。

sentences.en: It is something that has really only emerged in the past 15 years.
sentences.zh: 这确实是过去15年才出现的东西。

sentences.en: Before 20, I think it was like
sentences.zh: 在20，我想大概是

sentences.en: 2010, 2012, the talking stage was not really part of our vocab.
sentences.zh: 2010年、2012年之前，暧昧期并不是我们词汇的一部分。

sentences.en: It wasn't really a term.
sentences.zh: 它并不是一个真正的术语。

sentences.en: It wasn't really part of the early dating period.
sentences.zh: 它并不是早期约会阶段的一部分。

sentences.en: The reason why people in this generation are spending more time in the talking stage is because this period allows us to assess compatibility.
sentences.zh: 这一代人花更多时间在暧昧期的原因，是因为这个阶段允许我们评估兼容性。

sentences.en: Yes, it does allow us to test if we have the same interests, if we communicate the same, if we have the spark.
sentences.zh: 是的，它确实允许我们测试我们是否有相同的兴趣，沟通方式是否一致，是否有火花。

sentences.en: It does allow us to tell, is this person a total asshole?
sentences.zh: 它确实允许我们判断，这个人是不是个彻头彻尾的混蛋？

sentences.en: But it's also being used to really protect us against pain and to also help us avoid the emotional sunk costs that would occur if we just dived in headfirst into a relationship.
sentences.zh: 但它也被用来真正保护我们免受伤害，并帮助我们避免如果我们一头扎进一段关系中会产生的沉没成本。

sentences.en: That is typically what we think a talking stage is meant to help us do.
sentences.zh: 这通常是我们认为暧昧期应该帮助我们做的事情。

sentences.en: But this same study really examined that an increase in the pool of potential partners has facilitated this rise in the talking stage.
sentences.zh: 但同一项研究确实指出，潜在伴侣池的增加促进了暧昧期的兴起。

sentences.en: The main culprit being dating apps.
sentences.zh: 罪魁祸首就是约会软件。

sentences.en: People want to keep options open because this, you know, availability of other people is so much more obvious.
sentences.zh: 人们想保持选择开放，因为这种，你知道，其他人的可获得性太明显了。

sentences.en: It's just this huge pressure that there is always going to be someone else out there who could potentially be better for you.
sentences.zh: 这是一种巨大的压力，总会有人在外面，可能比你现在的选择更好。

sentences.en: So people want to keep options open.
sentences.zh: 所以人们想保持选择开放。

sentences.en: People want to not settle down as quickly or, you know, choose someone.
sentences.zh: 人们不想那么快安定下来，或者，你知道，做出选择。

sentences.en: And the paradox or irony of this is that normally they're actually missing out on the person who was right in front of them who may be really great because you keep thinking that
sentences.zh: 而这其中的悖论或讽刺之处在于，通常他们实际上错过了眼前那个可能非常棒的人，因为你一直认为

sentences.en: someone better out there exists when the person that you were thinking of is completely made up.
sentences.zh: 外面存在更好的人，而你所想的那个人完全是虚构的。

sentences.en: It's a classic example of the paradox of choice.
sentences.zh: 这是选择悖论的一个经典例子。

sentences.en: We have too many options.
sentences.zh: 我们的选择太多了。

sentences.en: Dating apps are creating the illusion of infinite possibilities.
sentences.zh: 约会软件正在制造无限可能的错觉。

sentences.en: That makes it harder for people to commit because it makes the possibility of something better seem a lot more real.
sentences.zh: 这使得人们更难做出承诺，因为它让“更好的选择”看起来真实得多。

sentences.en: I think what's hard about this as well is that the talking stage and the emergence of this has only happened in the last 15 years and yet we're still comparing our stories of
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中困难的地方还在于，暧昧期及其出现仅仅发生在过去15年，然而我们仍然在将我们的约会故事

sentences.en: dating to the love stories of before.
sentences.zh: 与以前的爱情故事进行比较。

sentences.en: We're also facing confusion from relatives and family members who have entirely different perspectives on dating from when they were finding love.
sentences.zh: 我们也面临着亲戚和家人的困惑，他们对约会的看法与他们寻找爱情时完全不同。

sentences.en: The stigma feels very severe but it's because our reality is just simply different.
sentences.zh: 这种耻辱感感觉非常严重，但那是因为我们的现实确实不同。

sentences.en: Our families don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我们的家人不理解。

sentences.en: They think that dating is the way it was when they were getting to know people and so we're facing this dual frustration of being like well I wish it was but also it's not
sentences.zh: 他们认为约会就像他们当年了解别人时那样，所以我们面临着双重挫败感：一方面希望是那样，但另一方面它确实不是，

sentences.en: so understand that this is just something we have to deal with.
sentences.zh: 所以要明白，这只是我们必须应对的事情。

sentences.en: So this is what I believe.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我的看法。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you a hard and fast rule here.
